The ICC Men's T20 World Cup is a biennial world cup for cricket in Twenty20 International (T20I) format, organised by the International Cricket Council (ICC). It was first played in 2007 in South Africa, and the 2024 tournament marked its ninth edition. The eighth edition, held in 2022 in Australia, was contested by 16 teams, and was won by England who defeated Pakistan in the final.

The **2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final** was a [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") match played at [Kensington Oval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kensington_Oval "Kensington Oval") in [Bridgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgetown "Bridgetown"), [Barbados](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados "Barbados") on 29 June 2024 to determine the winner of the [2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup"). It was played between [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_national_cricket_team "South Africa national cricket team") and [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team").

India won the toss and electing to bat first, they registered a score of 176/7. In the second innings, South Africa managed to post a score of 169/8 thus India claimed the victory by 7 runs to win their second T20 World Cup title. [Virat Kohli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virat_Kohli "Virat Kohli") was named Player of the Match for scoring 76 runs off 59 balls. Following the victory, Kohli, Indian captain [Rohit Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohit_Sharma "Rohit Sharma") and [Ravindra Jadeja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravindra_Jadeja "Ravindra Jadeja") announced their retirement from T20I cricket.

The [2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup") was the ninth edition of the [ICC Men's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup "ICC Men's T20 World Cup"), a biennial [world cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_cup "World cup") for [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") in [Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20_International "Twenty20 International") (T20I) format, organized by the [International Cricket Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Cricket_Council "International Cricket Council") (ICC). In November 2021 as part of the [2024-2031 ICC men's hosts cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024-2031_ICC_men's_hosts_cycle "2024-2031 ICC men's hosts cycle"), the ICC announced that the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup would be played in the United States and the West Indies.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

On 22 September 2023, the ICC released the venues that would host matches across the tournament,[[2]](#cite_note-2) with the [Kensington Oval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kensington_Oval "Kensington Oval") in Barbados named as the venue for the final.[[3]](#cite_note-3) On 5 January 2024, the ICC announced the tournament's schedule, with the final scheduled on 29 June.[[4]](#cite_note-4) This was the second T20 World Cup final played at the stadium, after the [2010 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Twenty20_final "2010 World Twenty20 final").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

This was [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_national_cricket_team "South Africa national cricket team")'s maiden T20 World Cup final,[[6]](#cite_note-ESPNcricinfo-6) while it was [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_national_cricket_team "India national cricket team")'s third final, having been champions in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_World_Twenty20_final "2007 World Twenty20 final") and runners-up in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20_final "2014 World Twenty20 final").[[7]](#cite_note-7) Both teams qualified for the final unbeaten, with neither of them losing a group stage, Super 8 or semi-final.[[8]](#cite_note-T20_World_Cup-8) Before this match, India and South Africa had played each other six times in the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, with India recording four wins (2007, 2010, 2012 and 2014) and South Africa winning two (2009 and 2022).[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10)
